title: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork
subtitle: BBQ-spiced pork shoulder cooked until it shreds
excerpt: A pork shoulder rubbed with a smoky spice mix and cooked in the slow cooker for 8 hours until the meat pulls apart in long, tender shreds. Pile into rolls with coleslaw and BBQ sauce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pulled pork in the slow cooker is a simplified adaptation of American barbecue, where a pork shoulder is slow-smoked over wood for 10 to 16 hours. The slow cooker produces the same long, tender cooking at low heat without the smoke. A dry rub applied the night before builds flavour in the meat. The cooking liquid is reduced on the hob after pulling the meat to create a sauce.

content.text: The pork does not need browning before going into the slow cooker for this recipe: the dry rub and long cooking produce sufficient flavour. The shoulder can go in straight from the fridge. Use a bone-in shoulder for a more flavourful result; boneless cooks in the same time. Remove the bone once the pork is cooked: it will slide straight out.
Mix together the smoked paprika, sweet paprika, cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar, salt, and pepper. Rub all over the pork shoulder. If time allows, cover and refrigerate overnight.

Pour the cider vinegar into the base of the slow cooker. Place the pork in the slow cooker fat-side up. Cook on LOW for 8 to 10 hours or HIGH for 5 to 6 hours until the meat is completely tender and pulls apart when tested with two forks.

Lift the pork out onto a board. Pull the meat apart into shreds using two forks, discarding the bone and any large pieces of fat. Pour the cooking juices into a small saucepan and reduce over high heat for 5 minutes. Pour over the pulled pork.
Pile the pulled pork into rolls with coleslaw. Serve BBQ sauce on the side.
